caption: The drawing shows an overhead view of an estate labeled "M. Ward Estate 1860," with a dominant palette of greens representing grass, shrubbery, and trees. At the center is a large red-roofed rectangular building, surrounded by curving walking paths and multiple garden beds outlined in yellow and white. Various circular and oval flower beds are present on the grounds, one of which contains a small fountain. To the right of the main building, there is a circular area bordered by smaller trees featuring a raised mound with larger trees planted on top. The lower left section features another red-roofed building adjacent to a grid of rectangular plots, likely garden beds or cultivated fields, alongside a smaller green-square patterned plot. Decorative tree lines and clusters of trees in varying shades of green are scattered across the landscape. Text in blue in the upper right reads “M. WARD ESTATE 1860,” and in the lower right corner, “THE BLACKWELL SURVEY” appears above a measurement scale. The composition is organized and symmetrical, with paths neatly connecting the distinct areas of the estate.
title: M. Ward Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
